Little Traverse Bay Bands of Odawa Indians

The Little Traverse Bay Bands of Odawa Indians names itself Waganakising Odawak in a publicly reproduced2005 constitutional preamble. That document describes several local bands within one governmental body. Its community-published land-use history offers a complementary reading path, combining documentary research and elder interviews. These sources help readers distinguish a particular government and its local histories from a broad Odawa label. They do not supply a current legal interpretation or exhaustive history of every named community.

01

Local names and shared government

The reproduced preamble names local bands and emphasizes their shared governmental body. Readers can use those names as historical and community reading paths without assuming that every place-name identifies a separate present government.

Read the sources [2] Native Nations Institute, University of Arizona; reproduced Tribal constitutional preamble

02

A community land-use project

Our Land and Culture is a Tribal project with research, elder interviews and youth participation. The earlier selected-page review is retained here with its original date and limits; it does not imply a new full-book reading.

Community-published historical book with elder interviewsLittle Traverse Bay Bands of Odawa IndiansSource 1

Our Land and Culture: A 200 Year History of Our Land Use ↗

Publication: November 2005; cover says compiled and printed then, not the 2021 upload date

A tribal project combining documents and elder interviews, with youth participation. Its own introduction limits later history to Waganakising bands, including Beaver Islands, and distinguishes shared identity from specific belonging. Selected pages only; neither a full-book review nor current legal interpretation. Historical vocabulary and family records are not replicated.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Visually inspected cover, contents, illustrations list, introduction printed 4–6, acknowledgements 7, chapter opening 29, and summary 43–44 (PDF 1–8,33–36,55–56, including intervening illustrations).

Review recorded: October 21, 2026

Little Traverse Bay Bands of Odawa Indians: Preamble Excerpt (2005) ↗

A publicly reproduced constitutional voice names Waganakising Odawak, related local bands and their shared governmental body. This is a selected2005 excerpt, not a current code or complete constitution review.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Complete displayed PREAMBLE paragraphs, lines15–20, read along with displayed2005 date. Linked constitution, later amendments, territorial/legal implementation and database population fields not reviewed or adopted.
